metrics.attempts_note: 2 validate calls (1 error, then ok) before the first render; render call 1 (n=13) wrote a pptx but deterministic_ready=false; render call 2 (n=14) was the first deterministic_ready=true. 4 warm-coral renders and 3 thumbnail passes in total; modern-template took 1 refused render, 3 validates, 1 render.
metrics.wall_note: System clock 10:27:11 -> 10:35 for the whole journey; server time is negligible (validate <=0.17s, render <=0.51s, 10 thumbnails <=2.6s).
guessed_values: chart.type bar_chart (no enum; copied from the example)
submit_visual_review findings[].severity 'P2'/'P3' and category 'whitespace' (vocabulary not enumerated)
enjoyment_reasons: Fast, cheap loop: deck_id + patch repairs are a few hundred bytes and sub-second; changed_slides feeds slide_indices.
Catalog examples are copy-ready; I never hit an unknown-field error while authoring and the first render wrote a real 10-slide deck from a 6.4KB spec.
Default output is board-presentable: action titles, takeaway bands, source line, page numbers, highlighted last bar.

Lost points: the gantt timeline looked wrong while scoring 100; validator advice named knobs DeckSpec does not expose; the template swap was refused and needed content cuts on 3 slides; plan_deck and recommend_visual output was not usable as given.

findings.title: Timeline with end_date draws three identical full-width bars and scores 100
findings.what_happened: Milestones with end_date switch the timeline kind to 'gantt' style. The render shows one full-width bar per milestone (a point milestone 'Oct 2026', 'Oct 2026 -> Dec 2026' and 'Oct 2026 -> Apr 2027' are all the same length), no time axis, and unexplained bar colours. Bar length carries no duration. The slide scored 100 and the deck was deterministic_ready.
evidence: call n=14: slide_number 9 score 100, deterministic_ready true
/tmp/jj/j/a-coldstart/slides/img-1791016216822-9.jpeg
findings.expected: Bars positioned and sized on a shared time axis (2 months visibly shorter than 6), a point milestone drawn as a marker, or a finding saying ranges cannot be drawn to scale.
findings.suggestion: Scale gantt bars to their dates on a month axis; if dates cannot be parsed, fall back to dots and say so. Add a check that flags range bars of identical extent with different date spans.

findings.title: Template swap refused; render_deck_spec shows 1 of 10 errors and hides the root cause as info
findings.what_happened: Patching /meta/template to modern-template on the approved deck failed. render_deck_spec returned a single TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN on a 25-character lead ('Revenue is ahead of plan.'). validate_deck_spec on the same deck returned 10 errors on 3 slides plus 3 FIT.BODY_TOO_LONG infos that were the actual cause (e.g. 'exec-summary needs 310pt ... content area holds about 304pt'). The cause is severity info, the per-cell symptoms are errors. Fixing took 5 calls and content cuts on slides 1, 6 and 9.
evidence: call n=21: is_error, one diagnostic, slides[1].points[0].lead
call n=22: '10 errors, 3 infos' 15.7KB
call n=22: FIT.BODY_TOO_LONG info 'needs 359pt ... holds about 336pt'
findings.expected: One finding per over-full slide stating the height deficit and the cheapest cut, identical between render and validate.
findings.suggestion: Report the slide-level deficit as the error and fold the per-cell shrink findings under it; make render_deck_spec return the same finding set as validate. Offer a multi-template check (validate against [templates]) so a spec can be authored to fit both before either is rendered.

findings.title: Following the option_matrix fit advice made the overflow worse
findings.what_happened: FIT.BODY_TOO_LONG on the option matrix said to 'drop the option details or highlight_label, hide the legend (show_legend: false), drop the slide takeaway, or split the table'. I removed highlight_label; the needed height went from 248pt to 262pt and the error stayed. show_legend is not a field in the option_matrix item_schema. Restoring the label and dropping the three option details fixed it.
evidence: call n=22: 'needs about 248pt ... holds 239pt'
call n=23: 'needs about 262pt ... holds 239pt' after removing highlight_label
call n=24: 'no issues' after dropping details
call n=7: option_matrix item_schema has no show_legend
findings.expected: Each listed remedy reduces the deficit, ordered by points saved, using DeckSpec field names only.
findings.suggestion: Compute the saving of each candidate cut and list them with numbers ('drop details: -30pt'); drop remedies that are not DeckSpec fields for the kind.

findings.title: Validator advice names controls the DeckSpec kind does not have, and its own fix triggers the next warning
findings.what_happened: CONTENT_DROPPED on the timeline said body is not rendered in gantt style: 'move the detail into the label, choose dots or chevron style, or remove the body'. The timeline kind has no style field (a probe with style:'dots' returned SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD). I moved detail into the labels as advised; the render then warned BODY_TOO_LONG 'a gantt bar holds about 36 readable label characters' although the item_schema says label <=60. Other hints had the same problem: SPARSE_FILL 'cap the grid height (bounds / max_height_pct)', SLIDE_UNDERUSED 'pair it with a supporting zone using compose', TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN 'explain_deck_spec lists them' (tool not in the profile).
evidence: call n=11: 'choose dots or chevron style'
call n=28: unknown field "style" on timeline slide
call n=13: 'values[1].label is 52 characters; a gantt bar holds about 36'
call n=7: milestones 'Label <=60 chars'
call n=13: 'cap the grid height (bounds / max_height_pct)'
findings.expected: Remedies phrased in the fields of the kind I authored, with the budget that applies in the mode I am in.
findings.suggestion: Translate pattern-level hints to DeckSpec terms before returning them (for timeline: 'remove end_date to get dots, where body is shown'); state the gantt label budget in the item_schema; expose a style field or stop mentioning styles.

findings.title: plan_deck routes the brief's facts to the wrong slides and ignores the slide budget
findings.what_happened: With format deckspec and slide_budget 10, plan_deck returned 7 slots inside a structure with auto_agenda and two sections (10 slides only if agenda and dividers count; no budget_note). Facts were split on commas: '44.1, 45.9, 48.2' went to the executive summary, '41.0, 42.3' and '9-10 slides' to the KPI slide, the revenue headline to the chart slide, churn to the option matrix, and two of the three options landed in unplaced_facts. I kept the kind sequence and discarded the structure and the fact routing.
evidence: call n=5: slot answer facts ['44.1','45.9','48.2']
call n=5: slot problem facts include '9-10 slides'
call n=5: unplaced_facts ['re-platform storage tier ...','raise SMB prices 5% ...']
findings.expected: The five-quarter series kept whole on the chart slide, all three options on the option slide, instructions such as '9-10 slides' not treated as facts, and a note on how the budget was spent.
findings.suggestion: Split facts on semicolons and keep numeric lists and parenthetical groups intact; route 'three options: a, b, c' as one group; emit budget_note whenever agenda/dividers consume budget.

findings.title: recommend_visual ranks a line chart and bmc-canvas for a two-segment comparison and answers in raw vocabulary
findings.what_happened: For 'contrast monthly churn in two customer segments: SMB 2.1% vs enterprise 0.6%' with item_count 2 the ranking was line chart 0.9 ('trends over time'), comparison-2col 0.85, bmc-canvas 0.69. Candidates are pattern or raw chart names and the next_tool_call is a raw_json2pptx slide, so nothing maps to the DeckSpec kinds I was told to author. The preview image it pointed to for comparison-2col shows four bare words on an empty slide.
evidence: call n=8: name 'line' score 0.9; name 'bmc-canvas' score 0.69
/Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/assets/pattern-previews/warm-coral/comparison-2col.png
findings.expected: A bar chart or two-KPI comparison first, expressed as a DeckSpec kind with its example.
findings.suggestion: Return the DeckSpec kind for each candidate, suppress framework patterns unless named in the intent, and render previews from a filled example with title and headers.

findings.title: get_started points a default-profile agent at tools and documents it does not have
findings.what_happened: The 12KB get_started response lists get_capabilities, validate_input, preview_presentation_plan, generate_presentation and inspect_slide_images in falls_back_to and raw_sequence, mentions make_deck three times, and cites SKILL.md, QUALITY.md and WORKFLOW.md. None of those tools are in the 12-tool default profile and a cold agent has no such files. item_schema text also references explain_deck_spec and get_chart_capabilities.
evidence: call n=4: falls_back_to ['get_capabilities','list_templates','plan_deck',...,'inspect_slide_images']
call n=4: 'SKILL.md lists them all'
call n=7: 'see get_chart_capabilities'
call n=3: tools/list has 12 tools
findings.expected: Only tools present in the active profile, and the rubric inline rather than by file name.
findings.suggestion: Filter get_started and schema descriptions by the active tool profile; inline the per-slide rubric (it is one sentence) and drop file references, or say how to enable the wider profile.

findings.title: Text budgets are missing from the catalog and differ by template, so fit is learned by failing
findings.what_happened: Kind summaries say 'past its text budgets it degrades' without stating them. item_schema gives limits for some fields (next_steps, stat, decision, timeline) but none for kpi_snapshot, executive_summary leads/supports, chart insights or titles. The title-slide headline wrapped to 3 lines at 51pt and was reported only as info after validation. The same spec passed on warm-coral and was refused on modern-template.

call n=11: INPUT.title_wraps overflow_ratio 3
call n=14 vs n=22: same content, deterministic_ready true vs 10 errors
findings.expected: A character or line budget for every authored field, for the template named in the call.
findings.suggestion: Let list_slide_kinds take template and return per-field budgets measured for it; include title budgets (chars per line, max lines).

findings.title: A recommendation spanning two options cannot be expressed

With one flagged, the slide badged only 'Renegotiate' under a title recommending both. I reframed the three options as two routes to keep the slide truthful.

findings.title: item_schema is large and padded with undocumented synonym keys
findings.what_happened: item_schema for 10 kinds was 36.7KB. Item objects list many alias keys with no description (kpis: big, caption, change, comparator, delta, label, small, sub, trend, value, vs; milestones: 17 keys; next_steps decisions objects: body, caption, phase, step ...). chart.type has no enum, so I copied bar_chart from the example. The layout/pattern/notes descriptions repeat verbatim in every kind.
evidence: call n=7: response_bytes 36658
call n=7: kpis items properties big/caption/change/comparator/delta/label/small/sub/trend/value/vs
call n=7: chart.type 'e.g. bar_chart, line_chart, pie_chart (see get_chart_capabilities)'
findings.expected: Canonical fields with a one-line meaning each, an enum for chart.type, aliases omitted or listed once.
findings.suggestion: Emit canonical keys only (accept aliases silently), enumerate chart types, and hoist the shared layout/pattern/notes/source/takeaway fields into one common block.

findings.title: Findings mix index bases, path syntaxes and pattern-internal names
findings.what_happened: quality_summary uses 1-based slide_number while diagnostics use 0-based slide_index. Paths appear as 'slides[7].options', '/slides/8/pattern' and '/slides/6/pattern/rows/2/cells/0/shape/text'. Several findings carry only a raw path that cannot be mapped to a DeckSpec field (which option is rows/2? which row is rows/10 on next-steps?), and messages refer to 'values[1].label' rather than milestones[1].label.
evidence: call n=13: slide_number 9 issues BODY_TOO_LONG vs slide_index 8
call n=22: path '/slides/9/pattern/rows/10/cells/0/shape/text'
call n=13: BODY_TOO_LONG has raw_path only
findings.expected: One index base and one path syntax, always resolvable to a field I wrote, usable directly in a patch.
findings.suggestion: Always return a JSON Pointer into the DeckSpec (the patch path syntax) plus slide_index; keep raw paths as optional debug data.

findings.title: describe_finding and auto-remediation do not match the finding they are attached to
findings.what_happened: describe_finding CONTENT_DROPPED gave a generic description with severity 'review' (the finding was 'info') and told me to read fix.params.locator and fix.params.reason, which the finding does not carry. The SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD remediation proposes op 'replace' with value '<rewrite this field ...>' on the unknown field, where the fix is remove or rename.
evidence: call n=12: 'Read the fix.params.locator and fix.params.reason'
call n=11: severity info
call n=28: remediation op replace path /slides/0/style
findings.expected: The description to cover the emitted variant; the remediation to be an applicable patch.
findings.suggestion: Generate remediation per code (remove for unknown fields, with did_you_mean when close); align severities; add the gantt-body variant to CONTENT_DROPPED.

findings.title: Whitespace and orphan problems pass at 100 while a tidy-up triggers an underuse finding
findings.what_happened: The decision slide (both the 3-box and 2-card forms) and kpi-4up leave 35-40% of the slide empty, with the recommendation band floating mid-slide while takeaway bands elsewhere sit at the bottom; both scored 100 with no finding in the final revision. A title with '22%' alone on line 2 was not flagged. Shortening two timeline bodies to remove orphan words produced SLIDE_UNDERUSED 'covers 22% of the safe content area (threshold 22%)' on warm-coral, and nothing on modern-template for the same slide.
evidence: call n=18: SLIDE_UNDERUSED 'covers 22% ... (threshold 22%)'
call n=25: no diagnostics

findings.expected: Sparse patterns to grow or centre in the content area; checks that agree with what the eye sees.
findings.suggestion: Let card/KPI patterns fill the content height or anchor the callout band to the bottom; add a last-line orphan check for titles; fix the 22% vs 22% boundary message.

findings.title: No way to fork a deck: patching for a second template overwrites the approved one, even when the render fails
findings.what_happened: meta.template wins over the template argument, so the only route to a second template was patching /meta/template on the same deck_id. The refused render still committed the patch, and the later content cuts mean the deck_id no longer reproduces the approved warm-coral deck. The two delivered files differ on slides 1, 6 and 9.
evidence: call n=21: render refused
call n=22: deck_id-only validate already evaluates modern-template
render_deck_spec description: 'spec template > this > archetype default'
findings.expected: Render the stored deck with a different template without mutating it.
findings.suggestion: Add a template override that beats meta.template for one call, or a fork op returning a new deck_id; do not persist a patch when the call fails.

findings.title: render_deck_spec repeats 6-9KB of explanation on every call, and the first next_tool_call narrows thumbnails to patched slides
findings.what_happened: Each of 6 render responses was 8.5-11.5KB, mostly explanation_summary with per-slide alternatives that did not change, including on the refused render. On the very first render the suggested next call was render_deck_thumbnails with slide_indices [0,8] (the slides patched since validation) although no slide had been rendered yet.
evidence: call n=13: response_bytes 11477, next_tool_call slide_indices [0,8]
call n=21: 8998 bytes on failure
call n=18: 9747 bytes for a one-slide change
findings.expected: A compact response after the first render; a full-deck thumbnail suggestion until a full pass exists.
findings.suggestion: Return explanation_summary only for changed slides (or behind a verbose flag); track which slides have been thumbnailed and suggest the unseen ones.

findings.title: modern-template uppercases titles and nothing says so before pixels
findings.what_happened: On modern-template every action title renders in capitals, turning '€2.2m' into '€2.2M' and making two-line sentence titles heavy. list_templates compact for the template lists fonts and colours but no text transform and no content-area height.
evidence: call n=29: no caps or content height field
/tmp/jj/j/a-coldstart/slides/img-1791016361190-2.jpeg
findings.expected: Template traits that change copy decisions (caps titles, shorter content area) visible at discovery.
findings.suggestion: Add title_case/all_caps and content_area_pt to the compact template projection, and a thumbnail of a filled sample slide per template.

findings.title: submit_visual_review finding vocabulary is not specified
findings.what_happened: The slides[].findings schema is {type: object} with a prose hint '[{severity, category, description, location?, bbox?}]'. I guessed severity 'P2'/'P3' and category 'whitespace'; both were accepted without comment. The response has 'manifest_updated: false' with no explanation, and render_deck_spec returns no 'revision' field although the review tool refers to one.
evidence: call n=20: findings echoed with severity P3/P2, manifest_updated false
call n=3: findings items {type: object}
findings.expected: Enumerated severities and categories, and a note on what manifest_updated means.
findings.suggestion: Add enums to the findings item schema and reject unknown values; explain or drop manifest_updated.
